Data.Function_Help:
Adds the default '.pkg' file extension to a Use statement that lacks one.
Example: Use cMyClass -> Use cMyClass.pkg
Leaves Use statements that already carry an extension (.pkg, .vw, ...) untouched.
Data.SummaryText: Added '.pkg' extension to a Use statement

Data.Function_Help:
Defines the bare 'Select' macro indicator left behind when ChangeLegacyIndicators /
ChangeSquareBracketsIndicators modernise a legacy [Select] under eModernizeSelect. Splices a guarded
SELECT-macro definition near the top of the file (an IFNDEF-guarded Replace) - NOT a Use line, since
OldFMACCommands.pkg defines SELECT only via the REPORT macro. Scans the rewritten code for a bare
Select, string/comment-safe; run it with those two, or after. No-op when none is found or the
definition is already present.

Converts legacy Begin_Constraints / End_Constraints blocks into a modern OnConstrain procedure.
The ENTIRE block body (declarations, Get/If/Else and the Constrains they control, and any
Report_* lines) moves verbatim and in order into 'Procedure OnConstrain' (opened with 'Forward
Send OnConstrain') - nothing is reordered or moved out, since e.g. a Report_Index parameter can
depend on logic earlier in the block. Comments are kept, blank lines dropped. A block with no
matching End_Constraints is left untouched. Takes a whole source file as a string array.

Changes legacy Calc/MoveInt/MoveStr/MoveNum/MoveReal -> 'Move' command.
The legacy commands compiles but does not work with the Studio's statement completion.

Changes legacy Character command with function Character.
Example: Character 13 to CR -> Move (Character(13)) to CR

Changes legacy Current_Object -> Self
Replaces the legacy keyword 'Current_Object' with 'Self'

Changes the obsolete Decr command to the modern Decrement command.
Example: Decr iCount -> Decrement iCount

Migrates legacy 'Object ... is a dfTimer' objects to the modern cTimer: swaps the class, drops
Auto_Start_State/Auto_Stop_State/Timer_object, renames Timeout -> piTimeout, strips the OnTimer
params, and renames Timer_Active_State -> pbEnabled file-wide. Objects that need human judgment
are left unchanged, each marked with a //TODO comment. Takes a whole source file as a string array.
Replaces legacy DfTrue and DFFalse with True or False

Replaces legacy GetAddress command with function AddressOf.
Example: GetAddress of sVal to aAddress --> Move (AddressOf(sVal)) to aAddress

Changes command "IFNOT" into an expression
Example: IFNOT Found Begin -->  If (Not(Found)) Begin

Changes the obsolete Incr command to the modern Increment command.
Example: Incr iCount -> Increment iCount

Changes index-number references in Find / vFind / Constrained_Find /
Constrained_Clear / For_all commands from one index number to another,
SCOPED to a specific table. Useful after a table-index restructure
that renumbers indexes for one table.

Rewrites BOTH `Index.<N>` and bare-integer forms in these positions:
    Find / Send Find / Get Find      : the <N> after a mode keyword
                                       (EQ, GT, LT, GE, LE, NE,
                                       FIRST, LAST, NEXT, PREV)
    vFind <tbl> <N> <mode>           : the 2nd argument after vFind
    Constrained_Find <mode> <tbl> by <N>
    Constrained_Clear <mode> <tbl> by <N>
    For_all <tbl>
Data.SummaryText: Changed: index number in Find/Constrained/For_all commands
Data.ParameterHelp:
Three comma-separated values: the table name, the FROM
index number, and the TO index number. Example "Customer,3,5"
changes every Index.3 / by 3 / vFind Customer.X 3 ... reference
for the Customer table to use 5 instead. Both indexes must berecnum mode, which
is never modified). DDO form recognised: o<TableName>_DD and
o<TableName>_DataDictionary (case-insensitive). Other DDO
naming conventions need to be handled manually. }

Data.Function_Help:
Modernises a legacy global Indicator declaration to a Boolean global variable. DataFlex
Indicator declarations are always GLOBAL, so the modern form is a Global_Variable Boolean.
Example: Indicator User -> Global_Variable Boolean User
Multiple names on one line are kept: Indicator A B C -> Global_Variable Boolean A B C
Owns the "Indicator. Use Boolean" variant of 4538 (the DECLARATION). 4538 is a SHARED number:
the "Indicate. Use Move command" + "...without parentheses" ([Found] usage) variants route to
ChangeLegacyIndicators / ChangeSquareBracketsIndicators - hence the match-text on every 4538 tag.

Changes legacy Insert command to use the function Insert.
Example: Insert "," In sText At 2 --> Move (Insert(",", sText, 2)) to sText
If sOne Eq "A" Insert "B" in sOne at 2 --> If sOne Eq "A" Move (Insert("B", sOne, 2)) to sOne

Replaces IN command with expression operator Contains.
It also swap places for the two variables involved and adds paranthesis.

Changes legacy Left command with Left.
Example: Left sVar 5 to sLeft -> Move (Left(sVar, 5)) to sLeft

Changes legacy 'Indicate' to expression
Paired with ChangeSquareBracketsIndicators: THIS function does the deep transform but
deliberately skips lines containing Find/Send/Constrain - the sibling sweeps those up.
Run both together; this one then reports the bulk of the changes.
Examples:
- Indicate Found as True --> Move True to Found
- [Found] and [FindErr] indicator statements.
- [Found| Command -> e.g. If Found Command
- While [Not Found]   -> e.g. While (Not(Found))
- [~Found] begin -> If (Not(Found)) Begin
- [Found ~Found] Begin -> If (Found and Not(Found)) Begin

Refactors legacy DbGrid objects to a CJ grid class with individual column objects.
For each matching DbGrid object found across all selected files:
  - The scope is code within the legacy object, not the entire file.
  - Renames the class to the new grid class.
  - Converts the Begin_Row / Entry_Item list into individual column child objects.
  - Maps Set Form_Width Item N to W  ->  Set piWidth to W  on each column.
  - Maps Set Header_Label Item N to "L"  ->  Set psCaption to "L"  on each column.
  - Removes legacy-only grid properties: Main_File, Wrap_State, peResizeColumn, psColumnsID.
  - Removes the standard Entry_Display boilerplate procedure.
  - Preserves all other content (other Set properties, nested objects, etc.) unchanged.
sParameter must be a comma-separated list of 2 or 3 class names:
  OldGridClass,NewGridClass[,NewColumnClass]
Example: "cTrDbGrid,cDbCJGrid,cDbCJGridColumn"
If sParameter is empty, any class ending in "dbgrid" is detected, and the
standard DataFlex classes cDbCJGrid and cDbCJGridColumn are used as targets.
Returns the total number of grid objects transformed across all files.

Refactors legacy dbList selection lists to cDbCJGridPromptList prompt lists.
For each matching dbList object found across all selected files:
  - The scope is code within the legacy object, not the entire file.
  - Renames the class to the new prompt-list class.
  - Converts the Begin_Row / Entry_Item list into individual column child objects.
  - Maps Set Form_Width Item N to W  ->  Set piWidth to W  on each column.
  - Maps Set Header_Label Item N to "L"  ->  Set psCaption to "L"  on each column.
  - Emits a one-time TODO header reminding the developer that the invoking
    object needs a Prompt_Callback handler (peUpdateMode pattern).
  - The surrounding dbModalPanel and the invoking object are NOT modified;
    only the list object itself is transformed.
  - Preserves all other content (other Set properties, nested objects, etc.) unchanged.
sParameter must be a comma-separated list of 2 or 3 class names:
  OldListClass,NewGridClass[,NewColumnClass]
Example: "cMyDbList,cDbCJGridPromptList,cDbCJGridColumn"
If sParameter is empty, any class ending in "dblist" is detected, and the
standard DataFlex classes cDbCJGridPromptList and cDbCJGridColumn are used as targets.
Returns the total number of list objects transformed across all files.

Refactors legacy non-data-aware Grid objects to a CJ grid class.
For each matching Grid object found across all selected files:
  - The scope is code within the legacy object, not the entire file.
  - Translates known properties to their cCJGrid equivalents
  - Renames the class to the new grid class.
  - Removes legacy-only grid properties: Wrap_State, peResizeColumn, psColumnsID.
  - Comments out the Entry_Display procedure body; any color Set properties
    found inside Entry_Display are translated and placed above the commented block.
  - Comments out legacy-only grid methods with a TODO marker.
  - Column sub-objects are NOT generated -- the non-data-aware column structure
    varies per use case and must be completed manually after refactoring.
sParameter must be a comma-separated list of 2 or 3 class names:
  OldGridClass,NewGridClass[,NewGridColumnClass]
Example: "cMyGrid,cCJGrid,cCJGridColumn"
If sParameter is empty, any class whose name ends in "grid" (but not "dbgrid") is
detected, and the standard DataFlex classes cCJGrid and cCJGridColumn are used as the target.
Returns the total number of grid objects transformed across all files.

The naming style of data-dictionaries *objects* over time has changed.
The new style is:
  Object o<tablename>_DD is a c<TableName>Datadictionary
They also have a switch so you can keep on using the legacy style name which is:
  Object o<tablename>_DD is a <tablename>_Datadictionary

However before VDF12, this is how it looked:
  Object <tableName>_DD is a <tablename>_Datadictionary

This caused tremendous headaches as due to the extra "o" we ended up with name clashes
all over the place. Copying old code into new views/dialogs simply breaks and if your
codebase has mixed styles then the compiler will not catch that.
A code nightmare.

Examples:
  <TableName>_DD - o<TableName>DD (eDDStudioStyle)
  <TableName>_DD - o<TableName>_dd (neDDNewStyle)

Reports Only! Makes no changes to the source code.
Pass an array with *all selected source files*.
Audits every External_Function / External_Procedure declaration: flags Integer/DWord
parameters or returns whose name signals a pointer-sized Windows type (hWnd, lp*,
lParam, *size*, ...) that should be Handle/Pointer/Longptr/ULongptr, and String
parameters in an ANSI ("...A") entry-point wrapper that should be WString.
Already-correct declarations are never flagged. See the 'Other Log Files' toolbar button.

Data.Function_Help:
Reports Only! Makes no changes to the source code.
Check all files in the current workspace to see if they are used, else list them in a report.
Pass an array with *all source files*
Returns a list of unused files. See the DFRefactor programs: 'Other Log Files' toolbar button for results.
Alongside the report, a companion 'MoveUnusedSourceFiles.bat' is also written to the

quarantine sub-folder, so the cleanup is reversible. Running it is entirely optional;
the report's footnote points to the .bat and explains how to undo it.

Data.Function_Help:
64-bit modernization: rewrites the declaration type Address to Pointer (the guide's
named replacement for the native pointer type) - local variables, struct members,
Property and Global_Variable declarations. Whole-word and idempotent; never touches
AddressOf, fields, or a variable named "Address". Params/Returns types are out of scope.

Reports Only! Makes no changes to the source code.
Pass an array with *all selected source files*.
64-bit truncation audit: flags a pointer-sized value moved into a 32-bit Integer/DWord
(which silently truncates on x64) - either a declared Pointer/Address variable or
parameter, or an AddressOf() result, assigned into an Integer/DWord. Per-method scope.
See the 'Other Log Files' toolbar button for results.

Reports Only! Makes no changes to the source code.
Pass an array with *all selected source files*.
64-bit struct-padding audit: in each Struct...End_Struct, flags a pointer-sized member
(Pointer/Address/Handle/Longptr/ULongptr) that does not land on an 8-byte-aligned offset
and so needs an Is$Win64 filler. A struct with an indeterminate-size member, or that
already uses an Is$Win64 conditional, is noted/skipped. See the 'Other Log Files' button.
Report-only - apply the actual fix with DAW's "Structure Padding Helper" tool.

64-bit fix for the Win32 "long" calls that truncate pointers: rewrites
GetWindowLong/SetWindowLong/GetClassLong/SetClassLong to their *Ptr variants
(GetWindowLongPtr, etc.), which are pointer-safe on both 32- and 64-bit.
Whole-word and idempotent; skips strings and comments.

Leaves Use statements that already carry an extension (.pkg, .vw, ...) untouched.
{ SummaryText = Added '.pkg' extension to a Use statement }
Function AddUseFileExtension String ByRef sLine String sParameter Returns Boolean
// Locate the filename token - the word right after "Use ".
// Skip if there is no filename, or it already carries an extension.
// Insert ".pkg" immediately after the filename; indent + trailing comment are preserved.

Defines the bare 'Select' macro indicator left behind when ChangeLegacyIndicators /
ChangeSquareBracketsIndicators modernise a legacy [Select] under eModernizeSelect. Splices a guarded
SELECT-macro definition near the top of the file (an IFNDEF-guarded Replace) - NOT a Use line, since
OldFMACCommands.pkg defines SELECT only via the REPORT macro. Scans the rewritten code for a bare
Select, string/comment-safe; run it with those two, or after. No-op when none is found or the
Function AddUseOldFMACCommands String[] ByRef asCode String sParameter Returns Integer
Integer iCount iSize iInsertAt iLastUse iFirstCode iSelectPos iShim
Boolean bNeeds bAlreadyDefined bSeenCode bIsUseOrInc bInserted bSkipLine
// Fast reject (NO tokenising): this function only acts on a bare Select keyword/indicator. SearchArray
// scans the raw lines via the _HasBareSelectKeyword comparator (boundary-aware - it rejects Selected /
// Selection / Select_State) and returns -1 when none is present, letting us skip the expensive per-line
// tokeniser pass below for files with no bare Select (the common case). A Select inside a comment/string
// slips through here (the comparator does not mask) - harmless: that file falls through to the accurate pass.
// ONE ordered pass (tokeniser is stateful, so top-to-bottom): detect the modernised bare Select
// indicator (the reason to define the macro), note an existing '#Replace SELECT' definition, and
// locate the top-of-file insertion point - after the leading Use/#include block, else before the
// first real code line (so the macro precedes every use, and never lands inside a header comment).
// Per-file progress nudge; no-op when no panel is active. Mirrors ChangeDfTimerTocTimer.
Send Update_StatusPanel of ghoStatusPanel ("Source line:" * String(iCount + 1) * "of:" * String(iSize + 1))
// An existing '#Replace SELECT ...' directive (our prior shim, or a hand-written define) means
// SELECT is already defined in-source -> nothing to add. A REPORT-using file has NO such line
// in its source (REPORT defines SELECT inside the macro), so we still add the guarded shim,
// which the IFNDEF then makes a no-op at compile time. (Note: 'Use OldFMACCommands.pkg' is NOT
// a marker - it does not define SELECT on its own, so a file with only that line still needs us.)
// Detect the modernised bare Select indicator. Skip lines that are NOT real code - comment,
// blank, image page, or part of a multi-line string (the latter is where a multi-line SQL
// SELECT lives, per tTokenizer.bIsInDF23MultiLineString) - so such a 'SELECT' never triggers.
// On the remaining code lines, search the MASKED line (indentation + overstrike, position-
// aligned, with string literals blanked) boundary-aware: (Select) / Not(Select) / "to Select"
// all match, while Selected / Select_State / Selection and a 'SELECT' inside a "..." literal
// do not. Stop searching once found.
Move (TD.bIsComment = True or TD.bIsBlank = True or TD.bIsInImage = True or TD.bIsInDF23MultiLineString = True) to bSkipLine
If (bNeeds = False and bSkipLine = False) Begin
Get _FindKeywordPos (TD.sIndentation + TD.sOverstrikeLine) CS_Select True 1 to iSelectPos
Else If (TD.bIsComment = False and TD.bIsBlank = False) Begin
// No bare Select anywhere -> nothing to do. Already defined -> idempotent no-op.
// The guarded SELECT-macro shim to splice in: a // comment + the IFNDEF/Replace/ENDIF block. The
// IFNDEF guard makes it idempotent and conflict-free (a no-op in a file that already defines SELECT,
// e.g. one using REPORT). This REPLACES the old 'Use OldFMACCommands.pkg' line, which only made
// REPORT available and did NOT define bare SELECT on its own. The #Replace line comes from
// CS_SelectMacroDefineLine - its |!C is built from Character() codes because |!C is a compile-time
// counter that a literal "|!C" in our source would evaluate here instead of emitting verbatim.
Move "// SELECT macro defined by DFRefactor (OldFMACCommands.pkg defines it only via REPORT); IFNDEF-guarded, a no-op if already defined." to asShim[0]
// Splice point: after the last leading Use/#include; else before the first code line; else top -
// always before the first real code, so the #Replace precedes every (Select) use.
// Insertion point past the last line (all-preamble file): append the shim.

Function ChangeBeginEndConstraint String[] ByRef asCode String sParameter Returns Integer

Move (sIndent + "    Forward Send OnConstrain") to asOut[SizeOfArray(asOut)]

// eModernizeSelect - by splicing a guarded '#IFNDEF SELECT / #Replace SELECT |!C / #ENDIF' shim near the
// top (NOT a Use line: OldFMACCommands.pkg defines SELECT only via the REPORT macro). The trigger is the
// FILE CONTENT - the function scans the rewritten code for a bare, boundary-aware Select token
// (string/comment-safe). The insertion tests assert the macro block is present (SearchArray) at the right
// spot rather than the exact comment text; the no-op tests assert the array is unchanged. ClearFuncLibProperties
// is sent first (as the engine does before every eOtherFunction) so the stateful tokeniser starts clean.
// Bare (Select) in code, a leading Use block present: the macro shim goes right after the last Use.
Get AddUseOldFMACCommands of ghoFuncLib (&asCode) "" to iResult
// The guarded macro block was spliced in, intact + consecutive...
// ...after the leading Use block, before the first code line.
// Bare (Select) in code, no Use statements, a header comment present: the macro goes after the
// header, before the first code line (never inside the comment).
Move "Object oReport is a cReport" to asCode[1]
Get AddUseOldFMACCommands of ghoFuncLib (&asCode) "" to iResult
// After the header comment, before the first code line.
Send Assert (iPos < (SearchArray("Object oReport is a cReport", asCode)))
// Bare (Select) in code at the very top (no header, no Use): the macro goes first.
Move "Object oFoo is a cBar"   to asCode[0]
Move "    Move (Select) to bX" to asCode[1]

Send Assert (iPos < (SearchArray("Object oFoo is a cBar", asCode)))
// Bare (Select) in code but the SELECT macro is already defined in-source (our shim present):
// no change, returns 0. (A leftover 'Use OldFMACCommands.pkg' is NOT a definition - that case
// still gets the shim - so the marker is the #Replace SELECT line, not a Use line.)
Get AddUseOldFMACCommands of ghoFuncLib (&asCode) "" to iResult

﻿    // Unit tests for Win64WindowLongFunctions - the line-by-line (eStandardFunction)
// refactor that modernizes the Win32 "long" calls that truncate pointers on 64-bit:
// Each test sets one source line, tokenizes it (Get Tokenizer ... populates the
// funclib's pTokenizer, which the function reads for the masked overstrike), then
// calls the function and checks the result. It is whole-word + masked: an already-
// converted *Ptr call, and a call inside a string literal, are left untouched.
Move "    Move (GetWindowLong(hWnd, GWL_STYLE)) to iStyle" to sLine
Get Tokenizer of ghoFuncLib sLine to TokenizerData
Get Win64WindowLongFunctions of ghoFuncLib (&sLine) "" to bChanged
Send AssertSAreEqual "    Move (GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE)) to iStyle" sLine
Move "    Move (SetClassLong(hWnd, GCL_HICON, hIcon)) to hOld" to sLine
Get Tokenizer of ghoFuncLib sLine to TokenizerData
Get Win64WindowLongFunctions of ghoFuncLib (&sLine) "" to bChanged
Send AssertSAreEqual "    Move (SetClassLongPtr(hWnd, GCL_HICON, hIcon)) to hOld" sLine
// Idempotent: an already-converted *Ptr call must NOT be re-wrapped - the left
// word-boundary plus the "Ptr" suffix stop "GetWindowLong" inside "GetWindowLongPtr"
Move "    Move (GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE)) to iStyle" to sLine
Get Tokenizer of ghoFuncLib sLine to TokenizerData
Get Win64WindowLongFunctions of ghoFuncLib (&sLine) "" to bChanged
Send AssertSAreEqual "    Move (GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE)) to iStyle" sLine
// Masked: a GetWindowLong( inside a string literal must be left untouched.
Move '    Move "see GetWindowLong(x) here" to sNote' to sLine
Get Tokenizer of ghoFuncLib sLine to TokenizerData
Get Win64WindowLongFunctions of ghoFuncLib (&sLine) "" to bChanged
Send AssertSAreEqual '    Move "see GetWindowLong(x) here" to sNote' sLine
// Multiple different calls on one line are all converted in one pass.
Move "    Move (GetWindowLong(hWnd, n) * GetClassLong(hWnd, m)) to iX" to sLine
